p0_findings: P0-1: The reviewed R1 filelist contains seven project-relative entries beginning with hw_autoresearch_nts07/, while the one-shot invokes VCS with cwd equal to a fresh private WORK directory below hw_autoresearch_nts07/results. With -f path resolution from the invocation working directory, all seven entries resolve below WORK/hw_autoresearch_nts07 and do not exist. The sole no-retry attempt is therefore exposed to deterministic compile failure before any of 960 workloads.
p1_findings: P1-1: The attempt token is created before lmstat, but the reviewed R1 exception handler publishes a failure quarantine only when WORK exists. An lmstat failure consumes the attempt without any failure quarantine. Compile or slot failure produces only a generic error JSON and does not seal phase/count state, the compile log, completed slot logs, or a raw-tree fingerprint.

P1-2: The reviewed R1 testbench has one negative alias attack, fixed to G96 chunk1 with base0 instead of base48. It has no G192 negative attack at chunk2/chunk3 for bases96/144. Positive G192 requests and oracle sensitivity are useful but do not satisfy the requested G96-and-G192 fail-closed attack gate.
p2_findings: P2-1: The future parser checks row/chunk cardinality and uniqueness but does not require output_tile to be in 0..output_tiles-1 or the exact Cartesian set. A tampered transcript with the same number of unique out-of-range tile IDs can pass this layer of parsing.

P2-2: The directed memory and integer oracle vary by global group, slice, bank and lane but not by output_tile. The separately checked weight_row_index protects the address port, yet arithmetic values alone cannot detect output-tile row aliasing; this limitation must remain explicit.

P2-3: The pending result schema does not directly bind runner/parser/contract/review hashes or the attempt manifest. A result hammer can reconstruct that chain from unique namespaces, but embedding the identity would make the sealed result self-describing.

positive_findings.acc24_and_commit: The wrapper retains a 4x6x16 signed Acc24 array across inner-engine resets. Every non-final inner commit is accumulated internally; external commit_valid and bundle_done_valid are final-chunk gated. The final accumulator is retained plus current inner Acc24 with a 25-bit overflow check. The analytical worst-case magnitude 192x16x128=393216 is below 2^23.
positive_findings.addressing: Header legality enforces group counts 96/192, chunk counts 2/4 and global_group_base=48*chunk_index. Request source channels are translated by base*16; weight_row_index is output_tile*source_group_count+global_group. Widths cover the frozen maximum row 1535 and channel 3071.
positive_findings.cycle_fairness: logical_cycle_count excludes passive W_HEADER synchronization but counts each accepted header and all W_RESET_ASSERT, W_RESET_RELEASE, W_LOAD and W_RUN cycles. The first accepted header initializes the count to one, later accepted headers increment it. Both axes use the same wrapper/load/commit protocol and physical G48 shape; only W_RUN scheduling differs.
positive_findings.fixture_identity: The reviewed fixture has 960 unique sample-layer-role workloads: 40 samples, four sequences with 240 workloads each, eight FC2 layers with 120 workloads each, 720 G96 and 240 G192 workloads. It encodes 115200 final commits and 1843200 per-axis integer checks.
positive_findings.provenance: R1 statically pinned 24 sources and its parser --static check passed before the author superseded R1 during this review. The attempt-before-license and no-retry namespace concept is sound, subject to the failure-evidence P1.

supersession_note: The author began an R2 correction in the same working paths after these findings were reported. Those working files no longer match reviewed_source_identity. This M2068 review neither approves nor rejects the moving R2 source; R2 requires a fresh frozen identity and the contract-selected M2070 independent hammer.
verdict: The M2067 R1 architectural core is promising and the frozen 960-workload identity is correct, but execution is not authorized. One P0 makes the exact one-shot compile path invalid, and two P1s violate no-retry evidence discipline and the requested G96/G192 negative-alias coverage. No authority pins or execution command are issued. The author's subsequent R2 corrections must be frozen and independently reviewed as a new identity.
